Notice that a materialist could say much the same thing. They could say that what is required for your survival is a non-branching material relation to some future thing.
This is a strange and surprising view. Here is one way to get your mind around it. Consider a case in which two roads ‘overlap’ in space.

My Division. My body is fatally injured, as are the brains of my two brothers. My brain is divided, and each half is successfully transplanted into the body of one of my brothers. Each of the resulting people believes that he is me, seems to remember living my life, has my character, and is in every other way psychologically continuous with me. And he has a body that is very like mine.

But here is an odd consequence of this view. Suppose that you wake up, and are told that you are the result of a hemisphere transplant operation. Next to you on another hospital bed is a body into whom the other hemisphere was transplanted. You do not yet know whether that body will awake.
Screenshot 2024-03-05 at 9.19.30 AM.png
Here’s a quite different way of responding to My Division. Recall this option:
Let’s call the resulting people Lefty and Righty. Then we seem to have four options:
You think that you know that you are the person you remember being. But, if that other body survives to become a living person, you will not be the person you remember being.

This also gives the psychological theorist the resources to resist the Teletransportation Argument. On this kind of view, premises (1) and (2) are false, because the psychological connections to Marsy and Venusy are branching connections.
You survive as A.
You survive as B.
You survive as both A and B.
You do not survive.

Just as I exist in separate locations by having separate spatial parts in those distinct locations, so I exist at different times by having different temporal parts in those different times.
Notice that a materialist could say much the same thing. They could say that what is required for your survival is a non-branching material relation to some future thing.
This is a strange and surprising view. Here is one way to get your mind around it. Consider a case in which two roads ‘overlap’ in space.

My Division. My body is fatally injured, as are the brains of my two brothers. My brain is divided, and each half is successfully transplanted into the body of one of my brothers. Each of the resulting people believes that he is me, seems to remember living my life, has my character, and is in every other way psychologically continuous with me. And he has a body that is very like mine.

You think that you know that you are the person you remember being. But, if that other body survives to become a living person, you will not be the person you remember being.

This also gives the psychological theorist the resources to resist the Teletransportation Argument. On this kind of view, premises (1) and (2) are false, because the psychological connections to Marsy and Venusy are branching connections.
You survive as A.
You survive as B.
You survive as both A and B.
You do not survive.

This kind of view - on which survival is a matter of having different temporal parts at different times - is called four dimensionalism.

One can describe this situation in a way which makes it seem mysterious. I-90 and I-94 are separate highways; the stretch of highway north of 65th street is one highway; and yet it is identical to both I-90 and I-94. How can this be???
Parfit argues that none of (1)-(3) can be true. So, he thinks, we are stuck with option (4): you do not survive.
